subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document a supported split-host public mobile `wss://` pairing pattern where browser/operator access stays behind SSO/OIDC and a separate mobile hostname uses OpenClaw token plus device-pair bootstrap auth?
rationale: The remaining work defines a public Gateway exposure boundary and could either clarify or weaken trusted-proxy expectations, so automation should not choose the supported trust model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
options.body: Add an advanced, security-reviewed docs recipe that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while documenting the dedicated mobile hostname, no browser SSO redirect on that host, token/device bootstrap auth, `trustedProxies`, `allowedOrigins`, and validation steps.

options.title: Keep Public Mobile Pairing Operator-Managed
options.body: Leave docs focused on Tailscale Serve, trusted-proxy auth, and the general exposure runbook while treating split public mobile pairing as an unsupported advanced deployment.

options.title: Defer Until Release Confirmation
options.body: Wait to document the advanced recipe until maintainers confirm the QR and route-list fixes are in the distributed iOS/App Store path and decide how to message known fixed-build behavior.

recommendation.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
recommendation.body: Add an advanced, security-reviewed docs recipe that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while documenting the dedicated mobile hostname, no browser SSO redirect on that host, token/device bootstrap auth, `trustedProxies`, `allowedOrigins`, and validation steps.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest owner signal from the route-list fix, the QR repair merge, and adjacent security-sensitive mobile pairing history.
